goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:144 — [P2, confidence 75] `(website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length)` classifies same-registrable-domain hosts by label count, so `www.example.com/user` on `forum.meta.example.com` returns only `www.example.com` and fails to show the path the task requires.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a logic flaw. Looking at the code on line 144-145: when `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` AND `discourse_host.split('.').length > 2`, it compares the domains. However, if `www.example.com` (3 parts) is compared against `forum.meta.example.com` (4 parts), the length check fails (3 != 4), so it falls through to the else branch which checks `discourse_host.ends_with?('.' << website_host)`. Since `forum.meta.example.com` does not end with `.www.example.com`, it returns just `website_host` without the path. This is a valid edge case bug where the path would not be shown when it should be for same-registrable-domain scenarios.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — [P2, confidence 75] `if website_host == discourse_host` performs a case-sensitive hostname comparison, so the valid URL `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` on an `example.com` instance returns only the host instead of its path despite referring to the same domain.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the code at line 141 uses `website_host == discourse_host` which is a case-sensitive string comparison. Looking at the diff, `website_host` comes from `URI(website.to_s).host` and `discourse_host` comes from `Discourse.current_hostname`. If a user enters 'http://EXAMPLE.com/user' and the instance is 'example.com', the comparison would fail because 'EXAMPLE.com' != 'example.com', causing the code to fall through to other branches and potentially return just the host instead of including the path. This is a valid edge case bug since hostnames should be compared case-insensitively per RFC standards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:43 — [P1, confidence 100] `:website_name,` adds a public serializer field without the existing `untrusted_attributes :website` restriction, so anonymous visitors to a trust-level-0 user's profile receive the website hostname and path after the `website` privacy gate deliberately omits the URL.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `website_name` is added to the serializer's attributes list (line 43) without being included in the `untrusted_attributes` call that protects `website`. Looking at the code, `untrusted_attributes` is a method that restricts certain fields from being shown to anonymous/untrusted users. The `website` field is protected by `untrusted_attributes :website` (visible in the existing code structure), but `website_name` is added as a regular attribute without this protection. This means `website_name` (which contains the hostname and potentially path) would be exposed to anonymous users even when `website` is hidden, creating a privacy bypass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:145 — [P2, confidence 75] `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host) ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host` changes the stated same-instance-domain UX objective without recorded human acceptance by exposing the full path for a parent domain (`example.com` on `forums.example.com`), which is not the same domain specified by the task.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims this behavior 'changes the stated same-instance-domain UX objective without recorded human acceptance.' However, looking at the diff, the test case explicitly tests this exact behavior: 'it returns complete website path when website domain is parent of instance domain' with Discourse.stubs(:current_hostname).returns('forums.example.com') expecting 'example.com/user'. This shows the behavior is intentional and tested, not an unaccepted deviation. The finding mischaracterizes documented, tested functionality as an unauthorized change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:105 — [P2, confidence 100] The new `:website_name` attribute at line 43 is omitted from `untrusted_attributes :bio_raw, ... :website, ...`, so anonymous requests that `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is meant to protect still receive the profile website’s host and, for same-domain URLs, its full private path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `website_name` is added to the serializer attributes at line 43, but looking at the `untrusted_attributes` call (lines 7-8 in the original), `website` is listed there but `website_name` is not added. The `untrusted_attributes` method controls which fields are hidden when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` returns true. Since `website_name` is derived from `website` (which IS an untrusted attribute), this creates an information leak where the website hostname (and potentially full path for same-domain URLs) would be exposed to anonymous users even when the website field itself is restricted. This is a real security bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11 — [P2, confidence 100] The anonymous-privacy assertion's `untrusted_attributes` omits the new `website_name`, so the suite stays green while the serializer's `include_website_name` exposes a TL0 user's hidden website domain to anonymous visitors.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real security concern. Looking at the diff, `website_name` is added to the serializer's attributes list (line 43 in user_serializer.rb) alongside `website`. The `include_website_name` method only checks `website.present?` without considering trust level restrictions. The `untrusted_attributes` mechanism (visible at line 40 with `def self.untrusted_attributes(*attrs)`) is used to hide certain attributes from anonymous/untrusted viewers, but `website_name` was not added to this list while `website` presumably is. This means anonymous visitors could see the website domain via `website_name` even when `website` itself is hidden due to trust level restrictions. The test file doesn't verify this privacy constraint for the new attribute.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:77 — [P2, confidence 75] The new tests assert only `json[:website_name]` and never render `{{model.website_name}}`, so a client model-binding regression hides the required URL path from profile visitors while every added serializer spec passes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a 'client model-binding regression' but the diff clearly shows the template was updated to use `model.website_name` instead of `websiteName`, and the serializer now provides `website_name` which will be automatically available on the model through the REST API response. The template changes in user.hbs (lines 66-72) properly reference `model.website_name` which corresponds to the `website_name` attribute added to the serializer. There is no regression - the client-side computed property was removed because the server now provides this data directly.
